children: Herbalife is searching for a new chief executive, as Stephan Gratziani is set to step down from the company's top role, effective Oct. 31.
Following the transition, Gratziani will remain a consultant focused on strategy and business development, the health and wellness company said Monday.
Herbalife's board has formed a committee to oversee the succession process for Gratziani. In the meantime, John DeSimone, the company finance chief, will serve as interim CEO beginning Nov. 1.

The succession plan comes after Herbalife said earlier this month that DeSimone plans to retire at the end of the year, with Scott Schaefer, the company's senior vice president of finance and transformation, succeeding him as CFO.

Gratziani joined Herbalife as chief strategy officer in August 2023, under an initial two-and-a-half-year agreement. He helped helm a turnaround that has seen the company return to growth, following a challenging postpandemic period, Herbalife said.

"Over the past several years, we have established a clear strategy and strengthened the company's focus on our distributors and the markets they serve," Gratziani said. "With the business now having returned to growth and a strong foundation in place, this is the right time for the company to enter its next phase."
